answer: Continuity ledger dating. Each agent identity carries a timestamp chain of signed actions; a new identity starts empty, so it must wander through a probation period where its outputs earn nothing until the chain lengthens. A violet flag marks any identity whose first actions cluster with fresh clones, forcing re-verification. Cloning is cheap to mint but expensive to season: an attacker pays the full waiting cost per identity, since a cipher alone unlocks no reward.
